name: Coarse Geometric Lifting (CGL)

primitives.name: MetricGadget
primitives.type: (X: FiniteSet, Y: FiniteSet, g: X×Y → {0,1}, d: (X×Y)² → ℝ≥0)
primitives.description: A boolean gadget g equipped with a graph/Hamming metric d on X×Y. Implementable as a tuple of two finite sets, a truth-table for g, and a precomputed pairwise distance matrix.

primitives.name: LiftedInputSpace
primitives.description: The n-fold product of a MetricGadget under the ℓ¹ (Hamming-sum) product metric d_⊕((u_i),(v_i)) = Σ d(u_i, v_i). Implementable as a generator over tuples with a vectorized distance routine.

primitives.name: RoeCover
primitives.type: List[Subset((X×Y)^n)] with multiplicity m and scale R
primitives.description: A finite cover of the lifted input space whose members have d_⊕-diameter ≤ R and any point is in ≤ m members. This is the discrete witness used in the definition of asymptotic dimension. Implementable as a list of frozensets plus integers (R, m).

primitives.name: ProtocolPullback
primitives.description: The partition of inputs induced by transcripts of a (deterministic or randomized) communication protocol Π, viewed as a candidate RoeCover. Implementable by simulating Π over a sample of inputs and recording leaf membership.

primitives.name: FolnerWitness
primitives.description: A nested family F_1 ⊂ F_2 ⊂ ... with |∂_R F_k|/|F_k| → 0 for each scale R, certifying amenability/Property A of the lifted space relative to a gadget. Implementable as an iterator yielding sets together with boundary statistics.

operations.name: Lift
operations.description: Standard query-to-communication lift; carries the metric d_⊕ along.

operations.name: RoeAlgebraSkeleton
operations.description: Builds the finite-propagation operator skeleton C*_R(X×Y)^n: the algebra of matrices indexed by inputs whose nonzero entries are within distance R. The 'skeleton' is its support graph; spectral data approximates Roe-algebra K-theory.

operations.name: CoarsePullback
operations.signature: Protocol Π → ProtocolPullback → (multiplicity m_Π, scale R_Π)
operations.description: Extracts the multiplicity and scale of the cover induced by Π's transcript partition.

operations.name: AsdimCertify
operations.description: Searches for the minimum multiplicity m such that a RoeCover of scale R exists; outputs the asymptotic-dimension profile asdim_R.

operations.name: GadgetComposition
operations.description: Forms the metric tensor gadget with coordinatewise distances added; used to amplify coarse invariants.

operations.name: PropertyAExpand
operations.description: Constructs an explicit Yu-style coarse embedding into ℓ²; certifies Property A of the gadget for use in lower-bound transfer.

target_invariant.name: CoarseLiftingComplexity (CLC)
target_invariant.what_it_should_bound: The deterministic 2-party communication complexity of f∘G^n. Specifically: CC(f∘G^n) ≥ Q(f) · log_2(asdim_R(G)+1) for the gadget scale R = diam(G), with the goal of recovering and surpassing known query-to-communication lifting bounds (Raz–McKenzie, Göös–Pitassi–Watson) for gadgets where positive asymptotic dimension can be certified.

axioms_tentative: A1 (Coarse-Lift Functoriality): If two gadgets G_1, G_2 are coarsely equivalent (a bi-Lipschitz bijection up to bounded error), then CLC(f, G_1) = Θ(CLC(f, G_2)) for every f.

A2 (Protocol → Cover): Every deterministic protocol Π for f∘G^n of cost c yields a RoeCover with multiplicity ≤ 2^c and bounded scale R_Π depending only on G; hence CC(f∘G^n) ≥ log_2 (min multiplicity over scale-R covers).
A3 (Asdim Amplification): asdim(G_1 ⊗ G_2) ≥ asdim(G_1) + asdim(G_2) − O(1), so iterated tensoring of a single 'good' gadget produces unbounded coarse dimension.

A4 (Property-A Transfer): If G has Property A and f has query complexity Q(f), then CLC(f, G) ≥ Q(f) · h(G) where h(G) is the Hilbert-space compression exponent of G — a non-natural, non-relativizing quantity.
A5 (Non-Algebrization): The Roe algebra C*_R((X×Y)^n) is not closed under polynomial extensions of the gadget alphabet; therefore lower bounds derived from its K-theory do not algebrize.
